original_question: Can the general problem of two meromorphic functions sharing four values be reduced by Zalcman rescaling to a limit pair with bounded spherical derivative without losing the essential shared-value data? More precisely, after passing to rescaled limits, can one rule out the possibilities that a value shared by the original pair becomes only a Picard value of the limit pair, that a value not originally shared by counting multiplicities becomes shared by counting multiplicities in the limit, or that the two limit functions collapse to the identical function, so that a proof of the (1+3) conjecture in the bounded-spherical-derivative setting would imply the general case?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.1—the paper’s (1+3)-conjecture for two meromorphic functions sharing four values, one of them counting multiplicities—together with the reduction question raised in the discussion around Theorem 1.3: whether the general case can be reduced by Zalcman rescaling to pairs with bounded spherical derivative without destroying the relevant shared-value data.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly targets the paper’s Zalcman-rescaling ansatz for the (1+3)-problem rather than the broader Four-Value literature. It accurately singles out the bounded-spherical-derivative setting from Theorem 1.3, treats it as a possible reduction step toward Conjecture 1.1, and identifies the same three failure modes emphasized in the paper: a shared value degenerating to a Picard value of the limit pair, multiplicity data changing in the limit, and collapse to an identical limit pair.
missing_details: The ambient objects should be specified as two distinct nonconstant meromorphic functions f,g:C→Ĉ, where Ĉ is the Riemann sphere.
The four shared values should be stated explicitly as four distinct points a1,a2,a3,a4 in Ĉ.

The underlying target conjecture is specifically the (1+3)-situation of Conjecture 1.1: one of the four values is shared counting multiplicities, while the other three are only assumed shared ignoring multiplicities.
The goal of the reduction should be tied to the full conclusion of Nevanlinna’s Four-Value-Theorem for the original pair, not just to preservation of some vague 'shared-value data.'
The limit pair should be described as a nonconstant Zalcman/Yosida rescaling limit pair (f̂,ĝ) with bounded spherical derivatives on C.

The three obstructions must be stated as obstructions to deducing the general (1+3)-conjecture from the bounded-spherical-derivative case: loss of a genuinely shared value to a Picard value, artificial gain of CM-sharing, and collapse f̂≡ĝ.
To stay close to Proposition 1.2 and Theorem 1.3, the auxiliary framework involving Φf, Φg, and Mues’ function Ψ should be acknowledged, since Theorem 1.3 is phrased in those terms.

The draft should make clear that, as the paper states, Theorem 1.3 by itself yields only partial information in the bounded-spherical-derivative case—most notably the cross-ratio condition (a1,a2,a3,a4)=-1—unless the above degeneracies are excluded.
refined_question: Let f and g be distinct nonconstant meromorphic functions on C that share four distinct values a1,a2,a3,a4 in the Riemann sphere Ĉ, and assume that one of these four values is shared counting multiplicities, as in Conjecture 1.1. Can the general (1+3)-problem be reduced, via Zalcman/Yosida rescaling, to the special case of a nonconstant limit pair f̂,ĝ with bounded spherical derivatives on C in such a way that the information needed to recover the conclusion of Nevanlinna’s Four-Value-Theorem for the original pair is preserved? Equivalently, can one rule out the three obstructions identified in the paper: that an originally shared value becomes merely a Picard value of f̂ and ĝ, that a value not originally shared counting multiplicities becomes shared counting multiplicities in the limit, or that the limit pair collapses to f̂≡ĝ, so that proving Conjecture 1.1 in the bounded-spherical-derivative setting would imply Conjecture 1.1 in full generality?
justification: The draft is close to the paper, but the nearest paper-faithful target is not a broader open problem about shared values in general; it is the paper’s attempted reduction of Conjecture 1.1 to the bounded-spherical-derivative case handled in Theorem 1.3. Conjecture 1.1 gives the exact (1+3)-statement, Proposition 1.2 supplies the auxiliary-function setup used to analyze it, and Theorem 1.3 proves that in the bounded-spherical-derivative case Mues’ function Ψ is constant and, in the (1+3)-situation, Φf and Φg have the exponential-polynomial form needed for further analysis. The paper then explicitly asks whether Zalcman rescaling can make this special case sufficient for the general one, and lists exactly the three breakdown scenarios your draft mentions. So your draft is conceptually very close, but it needs the basic hypotheses, the target conjecture, and the intended conclusion made fully explicit.
